(a) Find Mighty's profit on the sale of a 25-meter cable.

(d) Find the maximum profit that Mighty could earn on the sale of one cable. Justify your answer.

\section*{Question 3}

Mighty Cable Company manufactures cable that sells for \$120 per meter. For a cable of fixed length, the cost of producing a portion of the cable varies with its distance from the beginning of the cable. Mighty reports that the cost to produce a portion of a cable that is \(x\) meters from the beginning of the cable is \(6 \sqrt{x}\) dollars per meter. (Note: Profit is defined to be the difference between the amount of money received by the company for selling the cable and the company's cost of producing the cable.)
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find Mighty's profit on the sale of a 25-meter cable.
\item[(b)] Using correct units, explain the meaning of \(\int_{25}^{30} 6 \sqrt{x} d x\) in the context of this problem.
\item[(c)] Write an expression, involving an integral, that represents Mighty's profit on the sale of a cable that is \(k\) meters long.
\item[(d)] Find the maximum profit that Mighty could earn on the sale of one cable. Justify your answer.
\item[(a)] Profit \(=120 \cdot 25-\int_{0}^{25} 6 \sqrt{x} d x=2500\) dollars
\item[(b)] \(\int_{25}^{30} 6 \sqrt{x} d x\) is the difference in cost, in dollars, of producing a
\end{itemize} cable of length 30 meters and a cable of length 25 meters.
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integral } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\begin{itemize}
\item[1] : answer with units
\item[(c)] Profit \(=120 k-\int_{0}^{k} 6 \sqrt{x} d x\) dollars
\end{itemize}
(d) Let \(P(k)\) be the profit for a cable of length \(k\).
\(P^{\prime}(k)=120-6 \sqrt{k}=0\) when \(k=400\).
This is the only critical point for \(P\), and \(P^{\prime}\) changes from positive to negative at \(k=400\).
Therefore, the maximum profit is \(P(400)=16,000\) dollars.
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integral } \\ 1: \text { expression }\end{array}\right.\)
\begin{itemize}
\item[] \(4:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: P^{\prime}(k)=0 \\ 1: k=400 \\ 1: \text { answer } \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
